opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building chips, modems and AI platforms; up 6% YoY.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling, legal costs and running the company; up 15% YoY.

footerNote: Qualcomm guided Q2 FY25 revenue to $10.3B–$11.2B and non-GAAP EPS to $2.70–$2.90.
oneTimers: Non-GAAP results exclude $758M of share-based compensation, $52M of acquisition-related charges and $1M of interest on a 2019 European Commission fine.

Operating expenses include a $15M loss from revaluing deferred compensation plan liabilities, roughly offset by a $15M gain on the related plan assets inside investment income — the two nearly cancel out.

The tax line includes a $164M foreign currency loss on a refund claim for Korean withholding taxes paid in prior years, partly offset by a $128M benefit from the foreign-derived intangible income deduction and a $19M foreign currency gain on a tax liability from a Q4 FY24 IP transfer.
otherDetail: Investment and other income of $243M, less $163M of interest expense, makes up the $80M outside operations.
pngFooterNote: Qualcomm guided Q2 FY25 revenue to $10.3B–$11.2B.

segments.name: QCT
segments.note: The chip business. Inside it: Handsets $7,574M (+13% YoY), Automotive $961M (+61%), IoT $1,549M (+36%).

segments.name: QTL
segments.note: Licensing phone makers to use Qualcomm's patents — very high margin (75% pre-tax).

segments.name: Other and reconciling items
segments.note: Nonreportable segments not in QCT or QTL; the difference between segment revenue and the reported total.

takeaways.text: Automotive chips grew 61% YoY to $961M — a sixth straight record quarter — while IoT rose 36% to $1.55B; together the two non-handset lines reached $2.51B.
takeaways.title: Cars are the growth story

takeaways.text: Handset chips set a record at $7.57B, up 13% YoY and 65% of total revenue, inside QCT's record $10.08B (+20%).
takeaways.title: Handsets still the engine

takeaways.text: Qualcomm returned $2.7B to shareholders — $1.8B of buybacks (11 million shares) plus $942M of dividends — and guided Q2 FY25 revenue to $10.3B–$11.2B.
takeaways.title: Cash back to shareholders

verdict: Qualcomm set a revenue record at $11.7B as handset chips hit a record and car chips jumped 61%, with licensing still throwing off high-margin cash.
